cards.front: Recall a key point about Production Planning & Quality
cards.back: Production planning determines the most efficient sequence of manufacturing operations.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Production Planning & Quality
cards.back: The plan lists every operation in order: material preparation, shaping, machining, finishing, assembly and inspection.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Production Planning & Quality
cards.back: Process selection matches the manufacturing method to material, quantity, tolerance and geometry.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Production Planning & Quality
cards.back: Jigs guide a cutting tool to the correct position (e.g. a drilling jig ensures identical hole positions).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Production Planning & Quality
cards.back: Fixtures hold a workpiece securely in the correct position without guiding the tool.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Production Planning & Quality
cards.back: Workholding devices must hold the part rigidly against cutting forces without distortion.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Production Planning & Quality
cards.back: Material preparation includes selecting stock form, cutting to size and deburring.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Production Planning & Quality
cards.back: Quality assurance is built into the plan: inspection between operations catches defects early.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Production Planning & Quality
cards.back: Time estimation for each operation allows total production time and cost to be calculated.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Production Planning & Quality
cards.back: Safety planning includes risk assessments, PPE requirements and safe working procedures.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Production Planning & Quality
cards.back: Setup time must be minimised for efficient batch production.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Production Planning & Quality
cards.back: The bill of materials (BOM) lists every component and material needed.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse engineering exam tips — production planning & quality?
cards.back: 1. For Production Planning & Quality questions, use precise design and technology terminology 2. Consider function, aesthetics, ergonomics, sustainability and cost in your answers 3. When evaluating, justify your design decisions with reference to user needs and specifications 4. Show your understanding of Production Planning & Quality through both theory and practical application 5. Reference real products and manufacturing processes where relevant
